subject: Stormshore throughput & error surge — RCA delivery and remediation checkpoint
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@stormshore.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@stormshore.io>, Stormshore Support <support@stormshore.io>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Severe throughput drop & spike in 5xx — urgent

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing a sudden throughput drop across our inference routes at ~08:45 PT and a correlated spike in 5xx errors. Traffic patterns are normal on our side; token volumes match previous runs. This is impacting checkouts (Rolling 5–7% error rate on /generate).

We need immediate triage and an ETA for remediation — our peak window is this afternoon. I've attached the request log and a short sample of failed payloads. Please escalate to your eng team and let us know the plan.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Head of Platform Reliability
Stormshore Commerce

Attachments: stormshore_request_log.csv (12MB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya@stormshore.io>
Cc: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@stormshore.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe throughput drop & spike in 5xx — urgent

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick heads-up. I've escalated to the on-call infra and model-serv teams (cc'd).

Immediate actions:
- Ben and Karthik will triage the logs you attached and check runtime metrics (KV cache, batching behavior, kernel failures).
- We'll enable fallbacks to the last-known-good model variant and open burst capacity in your region to reduce customer impact.
- I'll schedule an incident bridge and share dial-in details in the next 10 minutes.

Please confirm if there are any sensitive payloads in the sample that should be redacted from logs. We'll treat this with exec priority.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@stormshore.io>, Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@stormshore.io>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe throughput drop & spike in 5xx — urgent

Quick triage notes from runtime:
- Observed a sharp increase in memory pressure on the GPU pool serving Stormshore routes at 08:42 PT.
- Several LLM workers reported KV cache eviction cascades leading to repeated cold-starts; the controller retried requests causing queue pile-up and 503/504s.
- No obvious network egress error to Stormshore; traces show internal throttling.

Attachments: stormshore_request_log.csv (same file as sent) — I've filtered problematic trace ids and included a short table of request latencies.

Next steps I'm running now:
1) Pin Stormshore routing to the previous model build (rollback quantization change) — 10–15m.
2) Temporarily increase per-route concurrency and open dedicated burst capacity — 20m.
3) Preserve all runtime traces and export to shared drive for RCA.

I'll update in 15.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@stormshore.io>, Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@stormshore.io>
Date: 2027-04-19T02:06:00Z
Subject: Post-incident draft: root cause & remediation plan (v0.1)

Team & Priya — attaching the first draft of the RCA and proposed remediation actions. Summary below:

Root cause (summary):
- A recent quantization/packing change in model build 20270417 introduced an allocation pattern that increases per-request transient memory by ~18% on long-context jobs.
- For Stormshore's long-sequence checkout prompts the memory increase triggered repeated KV cache evictions. The eviction pattern caused high CPU spikes across the serving runtime's garbage collection path, creating retry storms and visible 5xxs.

Mitigations delivered (Apr 18):
- Rolled back the quantization packaging on the Stormshore route to 20270410 build (completed 09:55 PT).
- Enabled route-level dedicated burst capacity and adjusted concurrency caps.
- Cleared affected KV caches and rotated pods to drain cold entries.

Planned follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- Deep kernel/memory analysis and improved telemetry for cache pressure (Karthik / 1 week).
- Add pre-deploy sizing checks for quantization changes (Marissa / 2 weeks).
- Formalize automatic fallback to compatible model variant on memory anomaly (Ben / 3 weeks).
- Executive readout and credit request response (Hannah / 48 hours).

Attachments: postmortem-draft-v1.pdf, remediation-checklist.xlsx

This draft includes data exports (traces, allocations) and a short runbook for outage avoidance during future quantization rollouts. Feedback welcome — I'll incorporate and send v0.2 by tomorrow EOD.

—Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Priya Rao <priya@stormshore.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@stormshore.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-incident draft: root cause & remediation plan (v0.1)

Thanks Karthik — that aligns with what we were seeing. A few asks from Stormshore leadership:
- Confirm concrete timelines for the three deliverables you listed (we need a firm date for pre-deploy sizing checks).
- We will want a credit for the impacted period and a short executive readout (20–30m) tomorrow afternoon.
- Please keep all traces and the raw logs available for our compliance team — they may request additional artifacts.

I appreciate the quick rollback. Please send the readout invite to Ethan and our CTO.

Regards,
Priya Rao
Head of Platform Reliability
Stormshore Commerce

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya@stormshore.io>, Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@stormshore.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T16:40:00Z
Subject: RCA delivery and remediation checkpoint — Stormshore (STRM-2345)

Priya / Ethan — attaching the updated postmortem (v0.2) and the remediation checklist with owners and dates. Key points:

- RCA finalized: quantization allocation pattern + cache eviction cascade. (See attached PDF for evidence and trace IDs.)
- Actions completed: rollback (Apr 18), burst capacity (Apr 18), cache rotation (Apr 18).
- Actions in-flight: pre-deploy sizing checks (Marissa — complete by 2027-05-06), telemetry improvements (Karthik — complete by 2027-05-12), auto-fallback runbook (Ben — complete by 2027-05-20).
- Executive readout scheduled: 2027-04-23 13:00 PT (30 mins). Invite sent to Priya, Ethan, Redwood execs.
- Credit request: pending finance review; I've opened a ticket and will update tomorrow with a proposal.

Links & artifacts: 
- Postmortem (v0.2): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1StormshoreIncident
- Incident dashboard: https://redwood.app/docs/incident/STRM-2345
- HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/contacts/companies/STRM-2345

If anything is missing for compliance evidence, call me directly and we will prioritize. We will follow up with a closure note after the in-flight items land.

—Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft-v1.pdf (updated v0.2 included in drive), remediation-checklist.xlsx
